title: V0b plan rebased — strict additive layer on top of V0a (plan 2026-05-21-001)
body: Pre-lock review identified that the original V0 draft re-proposed work already shipped or in-flight in plan 2026-05-21-001-feat-capability-manifest-consumers-v0 (manifest loader = V0a F001 done; probe capability_id binding = V0a F002 in-flight; adapter registry capability_id binding = V0a F003 in-flight). This is the kind of plan-collision the orchestrator is supposed to prevent — two active plans claiming the same loader/probe/adapter substrate. Rebase: V0b reduces from 4 features to 3, removes the manifest-loader F001 and probe-binding F002 (now V0a dependencies), and narrows to genuinely additive scope: setup_steps[] schema extension + `dontpanic capabilities status` CLI + plan-lock advisory sidecar. Roadmap (2026-05-22-001) now explicitly identifies 2026-05-21-001 as V0a and this plan as V0b.

title: Schema change is additive on v1.0 — no v1.1 directory invented
body: Original draft proposed `claude/shared/schemas/v1.1/capability.schema.json` — that path does not exist in the repo and inventing it would fragment the schema layout. Corrected approach: add `setup_steps[]` as an OPTIONAL field directly on the existing `claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/capability.schema.json`. The `schema_version` const stays `"1.0.0"` because the change is backward-compatible (existing manifests without setup_steps continue to load unchanged). Agent-conventions VERSION receives a minor bump to flag the additive change in the upstream source of truth. This follows the existing convention where field semantics evolve inside the v1.0 schema + agent-conventions version bumps; a v1.1 directory split would require a formal migration plan.

title: No new `capabilities/` package — extends existing `capabilities.py` module
body: Original draft proposed `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/capabilities/loader.py` (a package). The existing `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/capabilities.py` (shipped by 2026-05-21-001 F001, passes:true 2026-05-21T20:06Z) is a single-file module. Python cannot have both `dontpanic_orchestrate.capabilities` as a module AND as a package without a deliberate compatibility-preserving refactor. Corrected approach: F001 extends the existing `capabilities.py` with a `SetupStep` Pydantic model and a `setup_steps: tuple[SetupStep, ...] = ()` field on `CapabilityManifest`. F002 CLI logic lives in a sibling module `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/capabilities_status.py`, NOT a `capabilities/` subdirectory. F003 sidecar logic in `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/capabilities_lock_sidecar.py`, also sibling.

title: ProbeStatus.PENDING semantics: needs_probe_implementation, NOT blocked
body: Original draft conflated two PENDING semantics: features.json said `blocked` means probes fail with PENDING; D003 said PENDING is informational. This is a real contradiction. Corrected semantics: PENDING means `needs_probe_implementation / unknown` — distinct from PASS/FAIL/WARN/ADVISORY and explicitly NOT a synonym for `blocked`. A capability containing only PENDING probes can compute status `ready` if its requires resolve. PENDING probes render as informational chip in text output and `pending_probes[]` array in JSON output. The closed set of capability-level statuses is {ready, needs_setup, blocked, not_installed, optional} — `pending` is NEVER a capability status. `blocked` is reserved for capabilities with at least one FAIL-state probe.

title: external_refs[] is existing substrate, not a future dependency
body: Original F004 draft said Plan 2026-05-20-001 F002 was `locked but not yet implemented`. Repository inspection: `external_refs[]` is fully landed in `claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/plan.schema.json` (v1.10.0) with required `kind`/`uri`/`sync` fields and the `sync` enum `none|push_status`. The category-adapter resolver and lifecycle hooks documentation are also present. Corrected approach: F003 (lock-time sidecar, renumbered from F004) treats external_refs[] as existing substrate. Sidecar reads external_refs[] AND new optional requires_capabilities[] together; maps external_refs URI schemes to registered adapters (V0a F003 substrate) where available; degrades gracefully when an external_ref URI doesn't map to a known adapter.

title: F002 CLI degrades gracefully; F003 sidecar depends more strictly on V0a
body: F002 (`dontpanic capabilities status` CLI) does NOT block on V0a F002+F003 completion. When probe capability_id binding (V0a F002) is not yet shipped, F002 still produces useful output via requires-resolution + setup_steps + a single advisory note explaining the binding gap. This preserves the property that V0b can ship value before V0a F002/F003 fully land. F003 (lock-time sidecar) is more strictly coupled to V0a because the sidecar binds capabilities to plans — adapter capability_id binding (V0a F003) is the natural seam where external_refs[].uri maps to a registered adapter's capability. F003 still ships value via the requires_capabilities[] path when V0a F003 is incomplete, but the external_refs auto-derivation only activates once V0a F003 lands.

title: Lock-time sidecar is advisory only — does NOT block lock
body: `evidence/required-capabilities.json` is advisory: lock proceeds even when required capabilities are not ready; lock output displays a warning chip naming the gap. Rationale: blocking on capability readiness at V0 would couple plan workflow tightly to operator-environment state, making fresh-clone, CI, and parallel-workstation workflows harder. Advisory-only matches the existing lock philosophy of `surface gaps, don't enforce them at v0`. Exception: unknown capability_id in requires_capabilities[] IS a hard error (operator-introduced bad reference, not an environment state issue). Future demand-driven addition may add `--strict-capabilities` flag; explicitly out of V0 scope.

title: objective_contract.json added; goal_type stays new_feature
body: Plan-level validator requires `links.objective_contract` when goal_type ∈ {parity, new_feature, migration, incident}. Original draft set `goal_type: new_feature` without a contract — would fail validation at lock. Corrected: added `./objective_contract.json` with three user journeys (operator-asks-what-do-i-need-to-set-up, agent-consumes-json-handoff, operator-locks-plan-with-capability-dependencies), ≥15 required_evidence entries, 12 non_goals, and a completion_test that names the firebase-dashboard concrete first-touch case. Goal_type stays new_feature (not infra) because this plan adds a user-facing CLI surface + JSON agent-handoff format, both of which justify a new_feature contract.

title: Pre-impl sufficiency file operator-authored after critical review
body: The canonical `dontpanic plan lock` gate requires `evidence/goal-governance/pre_impl/sufficiency-findings.json` for goal_type=new_feature, but the sufficiency auditor still has no production CLI wiring — `sufficiency_auditor.run_sufficiency_audit` requires an injected dispatch seam. This plan already went through manual critical review: the first draft had seven findings plus one deeper plan-collision defect, then was rebased to V0b with objective_contract, collision-free module/schema paths, corrected external_refs substrate, and clarified PENDING semantics. The operator-authored sufficiency artifact records zero remaining pre-impl findings and exists only to satisfy the current lock ceremony; it is not a generated LLM-auditor artifact.

title: Target project sentinel corrected after lock warning
body: `dontpanic plan lock` succeeded but the skill-applicability sidecar warned that target parsing could not resolve the Target block because the plan used `target_project: null`. The canonical host-local sentinel is `target_project: none` per the target parser guidance. Corrected the Target block before dispatch so implementer/auditor target context can declare Env: dev, Project: (none) cleanly. No scope or acceptance change.
